entry.title: Hexo Blog Setup Series No.2 - Deploying Static Blog to GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages
entry.content:
1. Deploying Static Blog to GitHub Pages

  1. Install hexo-deployer-git
  1. Modify the _config.yml file
    The _config.yml file in the blog-demo directory is the configuration file for the entire Hexo framework. You can modify most configurations in it. For details, please refer to the official Configuration Description.
    Modify the last line of configuration, change the repository to your own GitHub project address, and change the branch to main (note the indentation).
  1. After modifying the configuration, run the following command to deploy the code to GitHub (Hexo triple command).
  • hexo clean: Delete previously generated files, can be abbreviated as hexo cl.
  • hexo generate: Generate static articles, can be abbreviated as hexo g
  • hexo deploy: Deploy articles, can be abbreviated as hexo d

    Note: When deploying, you may be asked to enter username and password.
    If “Deploy done” appears, the deployment is successful.

    Wait two minutes, open your browser and visit: https://your-github-username.github.io, now we can see the blog content.
    Like https://Kobayashi-007.github.io

2. Deploying Static Blog to Cloudflare Pages

  1. In Workers and Pages, select Connect to Git under Pages
  2. Then log in to the GitHub account corresponding to your Blog repository
  3. Click Save and Deploy and wait for the deployment to complete.
  4. After the prompt “Success! Your project has been deployed to the following regions: Global”, visit in browser: https://Kobayashi-007.pages.dev, now we can see the blog content.
    • https://project-name.pages.dev This domain is blocked requires VPN to access. (This site does not provide VPN services)
    • At this point, you can set your <username>.github.io repository to Private
    • Cloudflare domain resolution takes 24-48 hours, or as fast as a few hours (depends on luck)
  5. If you have your own domain name, you can bind your custom domain here.

How to Use

Create a New Blog Post

  • Then use a text editor to edit the content in _posts/This is a new blog post.md, note that it should be written in Markdown format.
  • For detailed usage, please refer to https://hexo.io/zh-cn/docs/writing

After editing and saving the article, you can use the following command to generate a local page at http://localhost:4000/ for preview

After confirming everything is correct, use the following command to push the local article to the GitHub repository

3. Install Theme

1.1. Git Installation

  • Install the latest version of the theme in the blog root directory
  • For first-time use, you need to install the renderers for pug and stylus

1.2. Apply Theme

  • Modify the hexo configuration file _config.yml and change the theme to anzhiyu

1.3. Override Configuration

  • Override configuration allows theme configuration to be placed outside the anzhiyu directory, avoiding the loss of custom configuration when updating the theme.

  • If you are on linux system, execute the following command

  • If you are on Windows system, please manually copy /themes/anzhiyu/_config.yml to the root directory and rename it to _config.anzhiyu.yml.

  • In the future, if you modify any theme configuration, you only need to modify the configuration in _config.anzhiyu.yml.

  • Note:

  • Any configuration that exists in _config.anzhiyu.yml has higher priority, and modifying the original _config.yml is invalid.

  • Each theme update may have configuration changes, please pay attention to the update instructions, you may need to manually synchronize changes to _config.anzhiyu.yml.

entry.title: Hexo Blog Setup Series No.1 - Building a Hexo Blog
entry.content:
This article provides a detailed guide on how to build a personal blog using the Hexo framework and deploy it to GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages. The main content includes:

  1. Environment Preparation: Install Node.js and Git
  2. Configure Git and GitHub: Set up SSH keys, create GitHub repository
  3. Initialize Hexo Project: Install Hexo, create a new blog
  4. Deploy to GitHub Pages: Configure deployment settings, push static files
  5. Deploy to Cloudflare Pages: Connect GitHub repository, automatic deployment
  6. Basic Usage: Create new articles, local preview, publish updates
  7. Hexo Blog Setup and Theme Customization Tutorial Navigation - Click to jump directly
    This tutorial is suitable for those who want to quickly build a personal blog without spending too much. By using the free services of Hexo, GitHub, and Cloudflare, you can easily create an efficient and elegant blog website.

1. Prerequisites

  1. Domain name (Not required, you can use a free domain name, or the domain name assigned by GitHub.io or Pages.dev)
  2. GitHub (Required, you need to register a GitHub account)
  3. Cloudflare (Not required, you need to register a Cloudflare account to deploy your blog on CF’s CDN for acceleration, but you can also directly use the domain name assigned by GitHub.io)

2. Software Requirements

  1. Node (Required)
  2. Git (Required)
  3. VSCode (Not required, this is a lightweight code editor that can help you develop good programming habits)

2.1. Install Node

  1. Open the Node official website and download the Node installer that matches your system, otherwise installation issues may occur. Download address: https://nodejs.org/en
  2. Install after downloading, you can use the default installation directory C:/Program Files/nodejs/
  3. After installation, check if the installation is successful. Press win + R on your keyboard, enter CMD, then press Enter to open the CMD window, execute the node -v command. If you see the version information, the installation is successful.
  4. Modify the npm source. npm downloads various modules from foreign servers by default, which is slow. It is recommended to configure the Huawei Cloud mirror source. Open the CMD window and run the following command:

2.2. Install Git

  1. Go to the official website to download Git suitable for your current system: https://git-scm.com/downloads

  2. Install Git with default settings after downloading. It is recommended to use the default installation directory C:/Program Files/Git

  3. Click Start at the bottom left of the computer to see Git CMD, Git Bash, Git GUI.

    • Git CMD is in the style of Windows command line
    • Git Bash is in the style of Linux commands (recommended)
    • Git GUI is a graphical interface (not recommended for beginners)

3. Configure Git SSH Key and Connect to Github

Common Git Commands

3.1. Configure Username and Email

  • Note: Fill in your GitHub username, no quotes
  • Note: Fill in your email, no quotes
    Check if the configuration is successful with git config -l.

3.2. Configure SSH Key to Connect to Github

  1. Execute the following command to generate an SSH public key, which is used for your computer to connect to Github
  • Note: Fill in your email, no quotes
    When prompted Enter file in which to save the key, just press Enter all the way. It is not recommended for beginners to set a passphrase.

    Afterwards, open the .ssh folder in the user folder under the C drive, and you will see the following files:
  • id_rsa private key
  • id_rsa.pub public key

    Open the public key id_rsa.pub in the above image with Notepad, copy its content, and then start configuring the SSH key in GitHub.
  1. Configure SSH KEY to GitHub
    Go to GitHub, click on your avatar in the upper right corner and select settings. After entering the settings page, select SSH and GPG keys. Name it whatever you want, and paste the public key into the Key field.


  2. Test the connection, enter the following command
  • The first connection will prompt Are you sure you want to continue connecting (yes/no/[fingerprint])?, enter yes
  • If you see the connection information to your account, it means you have successfully completed the environment preparation.

3.3. Create GitHub.io Repository

  1. Click the + button in the upper right corner and select New repository to create a <username>.github.io repository.
  2. The repository name must be in the format: <username>.github.io (Note: The prefix must be your username, this is required for blog preview, you can modify the repository name later)
  3. Visibility must be set to Public to facilitate checking issues during the first deployment. Click Create repository to create it.

4. Initialize Hexo Blog

  1. Create a folder to save the blog source code (I chose the path D:/Hexo-Blog here). Right-click in the folder and select Open Git Bash here
  2. Enter the following command in Git BASH to install Hexo

  1. After installation, enter hexo -v to verify if the installation was successful.
  2. Initialize the Hexo project and install relevant dependencies.

  1. After initializing the project, blog-demo has the following structure:
  • node_modules: Dependencies
  • scaffolds: Templates for generating articles
  • source: Used to store your articles
  • themes: Themes
  • .npmignore: Files to ignore during publishing (can be ignored)
  • _config.landscape.yml: Theme configuration file
  • config.yml: Blog configuration file
  • package.json: Project name, description, version, scripts and development information
  1. Enter hexo cl && hexo s to start the project
  2. Open your browser and enter the address: http://localhost:4000/. If you see the following effect, it means your blog has been built successfully.

entry.title: Hexo Blog Setup Series No.0 - Complete Guide to Alibaba Cloud Domain Purchase - From Registration to Configuration
entry.content:
🎯 Campaign Description and Notes

⚠️ Important Reminders

  1. Campaign Nature: 1-yuan domains are typically first-year promotional offers for new users on Alibaba Cloud
  2. Renewal Price: The second year renewal returns to original price (usually 50-100 RMB/year)
  3. Eligibility Restrictions:
    • Limited to newly registered Alibaba Cloud users
    • Each user can purchase only 1
    • Some domain suffixes are excluded from the campaign

📅 Campaign Period

  • Similar campaigns run regularly, but specific rules may change
  • Visit Alibaba Cloud official website for the latest promotions

🛒 Detailed Purchase Steps

Step 1: Register an Alibaba Cloud Account

  1. Visit Alibaba Cloud official website
  2. Click “Free Registration” in the upper right corner
  3. Complete mobile/email verification

Step 2: Real-name Authentication (Required)

  1. After logging in, enter the [Console]
  2. Find [Account Management] - [Real-name Authentication]
  3. Select individual/enterprise authentication (choose individual for personal domains)
  4. Upload ID card photos as prompted
  5. Wait for verification (usually 1-2 hours)

Step 3: Find 1-Yuan Domains

  1. Enter “domain” in the homepage search box
  2. Go to the [Domain Registration] page
  3. Look for “New User Exclusive” or “1-Yuan Domain” in the “Promotion Zone”
  4. Or visit directly: https://wanwang.aliyun.com

Step 4: Select and Purchase Domain

  1. Enter your desired domain name (e.g., yourname)
  2. View available suffixes:
    • Common promotional suffixes like .top, .xyz, .club
    • .com, .cn occasionally have promotions too
  3. Add to cart
  4. Confirm the price is 1 yuan during checkout

Step 5: Fill in Domain Information

Required information:

  • Domain holder: Must match real-name authentication
  • Contact information: Regular email and phone number
  • DNS server: Use Alibaba Cloud DNS by default

Step 6: Payment and Confirmation

Payment methods:

  1. Alipay (Recommended)
  2. WeChat Pay
  3. Bank card
    After successful payment, wait 1-10 minutes for the domain to take effect

⚙️ Basic Domain Configuration

Check domain status
Path: Console → Domain → Domain List
Status shows “Normal” means purchase successful

DNS Resolution Settings (Optional)

If you need to build a website:

  1. Click “Resolution” on the right side of the domain
  2. Add record:
    • Type: A record
    • Host record: @ or www
    • Record value: Server IP address

Domain Lock (Security Recommendation)

  1. Enable “Client Lock”
  2. Enable “Transfer Lock”
    Prevent malicious domain transfer

❓ FAQ

Q1: Why can’t I see the 1-yuan domain?

A: Possible reasons:

  1. Not a new user
  2. Campaign has ended
  3. Regional restrictions
    Try using a different account or contact customer service

Q2: Can I get a refund after purchase?

A: Domains are special products:

  • Order can be canceled before real-name verification
  • No refund after successful verification and registration

Q3: How to renew most cost-effectively?

A: Renewal tips:

  1. Follow Alibaba Cloud renewal campaigns
  2. Purchase multiple years at once (sometimes discounted)
  3. Use coupons

Q4: Can I transfer the domain?

A: Yes, but note:

  1. Can only transfer 60 days after purchase
  2. Real-name authentication required
  3. Both parties complete through “Domain Transaction”

💡 Usage Recommendations

Short-term Projects

  1. Suitable for testing websites

  2. Temporary project showcase

  3. Learning and practice

Long-term Projects

Recommendations:

  1. Use 1-yuan domain for testing in the first year

  2. Renew early if it works well

  3. Consider multi-year purchase or transfer to other registrars for price comparison

  • Clean Interface: Modern interface with friendly user experience
  • Free Features: Includes basic DNS management, privacy protection, etc.
  • Quick Setup: Takes effect immediately after purchase

Suitable For

  2. Enter your desired domain name in the homepage search box

  3. Add to cart

Required information:

  4. Price reference:

.com domain: approximately $12-15/year

DNS Management

FAQ

entry.title: Introduction to PySpark Development
entry.content:
Introduction to PySpark

Spark is developed in Scala, and PySpark is just a high-level API for Python to operate Spark. The underlying layer still uses JDK to run Scala code logic.

Environment Preparation

Using python3.10

Install JDK

Since Spark is developed in Scala, it requires a JDK environment to run.

  1. Download JDK

    1. Visit https://adoptium.net/zh-CN/temurin/releases?version=11&os=any&arch=any
    2. Select the JDK version that matches your environment and download it.

  2. I downloaded: OpenJDK11U-jdk_x64_windows_hotspot_11.0.28_6.msi

  3. On Windows, simply double-click to run the installer.

    • Note: In the custom installation step, select: Set or reset JAVA_HOME variable.
    • If you forgot to select it, you need to manually add the %JAVA_HOME%\bin variable and write it to the PATH path.

  4. After installation, open the command line window to test:

    You can correctly see the JDK version we installed.

    • If the installation is successful but you cannot see the JDK version information, it means the JAVA_HOME environment variable is missing, and you need to add %JAVA_HOME%\bin to the PATH variable.

Install Hadoop

When Spark starts, it calls winutils.exe (a local tool provided by Hadoop for Windows) to handle basic operations such as file permissions and temporary directory creation, even in Local mode (single-machine non-distributed).

  1. Visit the path to download Hadoop: https://hadoop.apache.org/releases.html

  2. I downloaded: https://dlcdn.apache.org/hadoop/common/hadoop-3.3.6/hadoop-3.3.6.tar.gz

  3. Extract and move to the local installation directory

  4. Configure environment variables: HADOOP_HOME, and add %HADOOP_HOME%\bin and %HADOOP_HOME%\sbin to the PATH variable.

  5. Download winutils.exe that matches the Hadoop version (from winutils repository), and place it in the HADOOP_HOME\bin directory (e.g., D:\develop\hadoop\hadoop-3.3.6\bin)

  6. Verify

Install Spark

Office Bulk Deployment and Activation Guide

This document describes how to use official tools to download, install, and activate volume licenses of Microsoft Office.

1. Required Tools and Resources

Office Deployment Tool (ODT)

  • Description: Official command-line tool for downloading and installing Office
  • Download Link: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/download/details.aspx?id=49117

Office Customization Tool (OCT)

  • Description: Online tool for generating configuration files (config.xml) that define Office version, language, and other settings
  • Tool Link: https://config.office.com/deploymentsettings

Volume License Key (GVLK)

  • Description: Generic key for KMS activation. Please select the correct key based on your installed Office version and year (e.g., Office 2016, 2019, 2021)
  • Key List: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployoffice/vlactivation/gvlks

2. Operation Steps

Step 1: Prepare Configuration File

  1. Access the Office Customization Tool (OCT) link
  2. Select product, version, language, applications, and other settings according to your needs
  3. After completing the configuration, export the settings. The website will generate a configuration.xml file
  4. Save this file to the directory where the ODT tool (setup.exe) is located, for example, rename it to config.xml

Step 2: Download and Install

  1. Find “Command Prompt” from the Start menu or search bar, right-click it, and select “Run as administrator”
  2. In the opened Command Prompt window, use the cd command to navigate to the directory where the ODT tool (setup.exe) is located

entry.title: Building a Free Image Hosting Service with GitHub
entry.content:
Building a Free Image Hosting Service with GitHub

In the internet era, image storage and sharing have become increasingly important. Whether it’s writing blogs, sharing technical articles, or daily image storage, an image hosting service is a very practical tool. This article will introduce how to use GitHub to build a free image hosting service and accelerate image access with CDN.

What is an Image Hosting Service?

Image Hosting is a service for storing and sharing images. With an image hosting service, you can upload images to a remote server and generate a public access link, making it easy to use on blogs, forums, or other platforms.

Why Choose GitHub as Image Hosting?

  1. Free: GitHub provides free storage space, suitable for personal and small-scale projects.
  2. Stable: GitHub is a mature code hosting platform with high stability.
  3. Version Control: GitHub supports file version management, making it easy to track changes and modifications.
  4. CDN Acceleration: Through CDN (such as jsDelivr), you can accelerate image access speed.

Setup Steps

1. Create a GitHub Repository

First, you need to create a new repository on GitHub to store images.

  1. Log in to GitHub, click the + button in the upper right corner, and select New repository.
  2. Enter a repository name (e.g., image-hosting), select Public, then click Create repository.

2. Upload Images

After creating the repository, you can upload images in the following ways:

  • Web Upload: On the repository page, click Add file -> Upload files, select local images and upload.
  • Git Command Line: Use Git command line tools to push images to the repository.

3. Get Image Links

After uploading images, you can get the access link in the following way:

  1. Open the GitHub repository and find the uploaded image.
  2. Click on the image to enter the image preview page.
  3. Right-click and copy the image address (URL), which should be in the following format:
    https://github.com/your-username/image-hosting/raw/main/image-name.png

4. Use CDN Acceleration (Optional)

To improve image access speed, you can use a free CDN service (such as jsDelivr) to accelerate GitHub images.

Convert GitHub image links to jsDelivr CDN links:
For example:
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/anzhiyu/image-hosting@main/logo.png

Notes

  1. Repository Publicity: GitHub image hosting requires the repository to be set to Public, otherwise images cannot be accessed externally.
  2. Storage Limit: GitHub has a 1GB storage limit per repository. If you have many images, it is recommended to store them in multiple repositories.
  3. Bandwidth Limit: GitHub has certain bandwidth limits for repositories. If traffic is too high, it may be throttled.

Summary

Building an image hosting service with GitHub is not only free but also provides stable service and version control features. With CDN acceleration, you can further improve image access speed. Whether for personal blogs or small projects, GitHub image hosting is a very practical choice.

If you have any questions or suggestions, feel free to leave a comment!
